commits.message:
A joiner is a seam and caps picked independently (rich-joiners-9ntp.13i) (#406)

* A joiner is a seam and caps picked independently (rich-joiners-9ntp.13i)

CellJoiner takes a JoinSeam (the middle) and a JoinCaps (the ends), each
with its glyph and ascii forms, so any seam ends in any caps: SEAMS.prism
with CAPS.bubble is one constructor call, and joinerNamed reads
{ seam, caps } from config beside a JOINERS name. A seam cell may be
{ cap: "lead" | "tail" }, so the seams that part their runs (capsule,
wrapper, metro) end them in whatever caps they are joined with.
gradientSeam replaces gradientJoiner.

Every JOINERS preset and the gradient render byte-identically to before
(truecolor, 16-colour and ASCII, checked against a pre-change snapshot).

* Each part reads its own grounds; a seam's divider fits it under every caps (rich-joiners-9ntp.13i)

High review pass on #406:
- A seam decides its endpoints from the grounds the seam and divider read,
  a lead or tail from the one it reads, so caps that need a ground no longer
  stop a seam that needs none (plain + capsule dropped every " | ").
- parseSeam holds the divider to the seam's width under every caps (own cells'
  width and each cap's count equal), so a parsed seam is valid with any caps.
- A cell naming a cap and drawing a glyph is refused, not silently reduced.
- Refusals name the argument (`seam:` / `caps:`), not `CellJoiner:`.
- joinerNamed refuses a spec that is neither a name nor { seam, caps }.
- Private Use Area glyphs back to \u escapes, as master had them.
